governanceNotes: D1 batch 44 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - hemothorax to anemia (rank 1), ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory THROMBOTIC_OR_VASCULAR (intrathoracic hemorrhage). The proposition rests on the Heller 2026 multicenter pediatric trauma analysis, which quantifies hemothorax volume thresholds for chest-tube placement and therefore documents the magnitude of blood sequestered in the pleural space, and on the Morgan 2015 clinical review of spontaneous hemothorax, which frames hemothorax as an intrathoracic hemorrhage with systemic consequences. The edge is not raised to causation: the located evidence quantifies retained blood volume and management thresholds rather than incident anemia attributable to hemothorax, anemia in trauma patients is frequently multifactorial (bleeding at other sites, hemodilution, inflammation-driven anemia of injury, pre-existing deficiency), and no matched-cohort hemoglobin-decline data were located, so no probability estimate is asserted.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no pleural-effusion edge - retained hemothorax is a blood collection rather than a pleural effusion (entity guard), and the located complication literature addresses fibrothorax and empyema formation after retained hemothorax (Lyon 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of thoracic irrigation; Western Trauma Association multicenter study of irrigation to prevent secondary intervention), for which no catalog identities exist (wrong-target guard); reopen a pleural-complication edge only if a fibrothorax or empyema identity is cataloged; (ii) no unexplained-chronic-pain edge - post-traumatic chest-wall and pleural pain is plausible but no condition-specific quantification or delay evidence was located (zero-record guard); (iii) no cardiac-inflammatory-disease, cardiac-arrhythmia, or congestive-heart-failure edge - no condition-specific direction data were located for hemothorax-primary cardiac outcomes (zero-record guard); (iv) no pneumonia, empyema, or respiratory-infection edge - the relevant identities are absent from the registry (wrong-target guard); (v) no depressive-disorder or post-traumatic-stress edge - no condition-specific directional evidence was located, and the pain and psychiatric windows belong to their own primaries (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (vi) duplicate-scope note: this batch adds the first hemothorax-primary window to the registry, while the pleural-effusion identity keeps its two existing incoming windows.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Heller 2026 multicenter pediatric trauma analysis documents hemothorax volume thresholds that determine whether chest-tube drainage is required, and the Morgan 2015 clinical review frames spontaneous hemothorax as an intrathoracic hemorrhage - documenting that hemothorax sequesters measurable blood volume outside the circulation, a bounded hemorrhage-to-anemia association rather than an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the located evidence quantifies retained pleural blood volume and drainage thresholds without matched-cohort hemoglobin-decline data, anemia in trauma populations is frequently multifactorial (concurrent bleeding, hemodilution, injury-related inflammation, pre-existing deficiency), and individual determination requires documented hemothorax with drainage or imaging quantification, serial blood counts with chronology, and exclusion of other bleeding sites and non-hemorrhagic anemia causes.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized hemorrhage-to-depletion route is described: bleeding into the pleural space after thoracic or systemic vascular injury sequesters whole blood outside the effective circulation, and because the pleural space accommodates a large volume, the loss can be substantial; when the shed volume exceeds compensatory reserve or continues over time, circulating hemoglobin falls and transfusion may be required - documented by the volume-threshold management data and the spontaneous-hemothorax review - while the absence of matched-cohort hemoglobin data and the multifactorial anemia context in trauma leave individual attribution hypothesized.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Pleural inflammation from retained blood may contribute to systemic inflammatory responses that suppress erythropoiesis, and concurrent injuries, hemodilution from resuscitation, or pre-existing iron deficiency can amplify the observed anemia.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: the located evidence quantifies pleural blood volume and drainage thresholds without matched-cohort hemoglobin-decline data, anemia in trauma patients is commonly multifactorial, and bleeding at other sites and pre-existing deficiency are frequent competing causes, so an individual determination requires hemothorax documentation, serial blood counts, and competing-cause review; no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documentation of the hemothorax (cause, imaging findings, estimated volume, drainage procedure and output, date); serial blood counts with chronology relative to the hemothorax; evidence of bleeding or transfusion at other sites and resuscitation volumes; assessment of pre-existing anemia, iron status, renal function, and chronic inflammation; evaluation of anticoagulant or antiplatelet use; trauma, pulmonary, or surgical assessment of whether the hemothorax materially contributed to the anemia course
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Hemorrhage from other sites (chest wall, abdominal, retroperitoneal, long-bone, or surgical)
Hemodilution from crystalloid or blood-product resuscitation
Pre-existing iron deficiency, nutritional deficiency, or chronic inflammatory anemia
Medication-related blood loss or marrow suppression

evidenceGaps: Documentation of the hemothorax (cause, imaging findings, estimated volume, drainage procedure and output, date); serial blood counts with chronology relative to the hemothorax; evidence of bleeding or transfusion at other sites and resuscitation volumes; assessment of pre-existing anemia, iron status, renal function, and chronic inflammation; evaluation of anticoagulant or antiplatelet use; trauma, pulmonary, or surgical assessment of whether the hemothorax materially contributed to the anemia course
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: multicenter management data quantify the volume of blood that can be retained in the pleural space and a clinical review frames hemothorax as intrathoracic hemorrhage, establishing a bounded relationship between the lesion and circulating blood volume, but no matched-cohort hemoglobin-decline data exist and anemia in trauma populations is multifactorial, so the consensus remains NOT_ESTABLISHED with documentation, chronology, and competing-bleeding-source requirements; no probability estimate is asserted.
